### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every one of the 200 traces contained the same sequence of two activity groups: A30, then the group A33/A35/A36 (no fixed order among the three), then the group A37/A38/A39 (again unordered), then A31. In the later window, A30 and A31 still appear in every trace, but A33, A35 and A36 each appear in only about 46–47 in 100 traces, and A37, A38 and A39 in about 56 in 100. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, REL004, REL025]
- The two groups turned from sequential stages into alternatives. Before, A33 co-occurred with A37 (and likewise A35 or A36 with A37/A38/A39) in all 200 traces, preceding it in about 99 in 100 cases; in the later window such co-occurrence survives in only about 3 in 100 traces, while about 44 in 100 traces contain the A33/A35/A36 group alone and about 53 in 100 the A37/A38/A39 group alone. Each group still moves as a block (A33 with A35 in about 46 in 100 later traces, A37 with A38 in about 56 in 100) and keeps its internal no-fixed order. [REL013, REL015, REL017, REL019, REL022, REL025]
- Successors changed accordingly. Earlier, about 97 in 100 of A30's observed outgoing transitions went to A33/A35/A36 and none to A37/A38/A39, and A33/A35/A36 never led directly to A31; in the later window about 52 in 100 of A30's outgoing transitions go to A37/A38/A39 (about 15–19 in 100 each), and A31 receives about 26–34 in 100 of the outgoing transitions of each of A33, A35 and A36. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- Distances shrank accordingly: A30 to A37/A38/A39, and A33/A35/A36 to A31, typically spanned 4–5 event positions before and 1–3 positions in the later window. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG006, LAG009]
- Relative event positions shifted consistently with shorter traces: A33/A35/A36 moved later (mean about 0.68 to about 0.74), A39 earlier (about 0.77 to 0.73) and A31 slightly earlier (about 0.82 to 0.80); these are event positions, not clock times. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the segment between A30 and A31, which previously always executed two groups in sequence (A33/A35/A36 followed by A37/A38/A39), in the later window executes these groups as alternatives: roughly 44 in 100 cases run only A33/A35/A36, roughly 53 in 100 run only A37/A38/A39, and both groups run together in only about 3 in 100 cases, while A30 and A31 still run in every case. Equivalently, each of A33, A35 and A36 is skipped in about 54 in 100 later cases (never in the earlier window) and each of A37, A38 and A39 in about 44 in 100 (never earlier), with the skips complementary; A30 now often flows directly to A37/A38/A39, and A33/A35/A36 often flow directly to A31. [REL013, REL015, REL017, REL022, REL025, DIR001, DIR002, DIR004, LAG001, LAG004]

The support is direct rather than merely numerous: relational items show the co-occurrence collapse with a complementary one-sided pattern, DIR items show the new direct successors, and LAG items show the bypassed distance, all describing the same two-group alternation while group-internal order and the positions of A30 and A31 are preserved. The 48 qualifying control-flow items are far beyond the roughly 0.58 expected without a change, so chance cannot explain the pattern as a whole. [REL015, REL022, DIR001, DIR004, LAG001, LAG004]

Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish a within-case choice between the two groups from a later window that mixes two case populations (for example a newly introduced variant coexisting with the old one), and about 3 in 100 later traces still contain both groups, so the exclusivity is not absolute; a few LAG items rest on only 4–5 later observations and were not relied upon. [REL015, LAG005, LAG007, LAG010, LAG011]

Other differences: A30 gained several rare successors (A04, A08, A10, A20, A45, A46, about 0.5 in 100 of its outgoing transitions each) and its relative position moved slightly later (mean about 0.62 to 0.67); A33 and A35 also show rare new successors (A01, A05, A06, A02, A08). These are minor and not part of the main hypothesis. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, POS001]
